name: Perfetto v59.1
body: We’re excited to share Perfetto v59.1! This release brings **traces that survive device reboots** on Android, a much friendlier **Trace Processor command line** (rustc-style SQL errors, markdown output and a dedicated agent mode for AI coding tools), **flamegraphs as call trees and function tables**, **sampled callstacks over time**, a new **`linux.smaps` data source**, and a long list of UI, SQL standard library and SDK improvements. > Note: v59.0 was never released due to a build issue on the Linux and Android release builders. v59.1 contains the same changes plus the build fix. ## 🔁 Persistent traces across reboots (Android) Set `TraceConfig.persist_trace_across_reboots` and the trace file is kept on disk if the device reboots mid-trace, then recovered and uploaded on the next boot via `perfetto --upload-after-reboot`. Recovered traces record why in the new `trace_recovery_reason` metadata entry. ## 🔥 New ways to look at profiles in the UI Flamegraphs are great for spotting where cost goes, but they're only one way to read a profile. v59 adds two new views over the same data, plus a way to see how stacks change over time. - **Call Tree view:** every flamegraph panel now has Flamegraph, Call Tree and Functions tabs. Call Tree is an expandable table with total and self cost for every frame, shown top-down (callees) or bottom-up (callers). The tabs share the same filters, and switching between them doesn't re-run the query. - **Functions view:** a flat table with the cost of each function summed over every call path, the quickest way to answer "which function is hottest overall?". Recursion isn't double-counted. - **Available everywhere:** CPU callstack samples, heapprofd and Java heap profiles, Heap Dump Explorer, Day Explorer, the pprof (aggregate profiles) page and track event callstacks all get the new views. - **Sampled callstacks over time:** each thread with callstack samples now gets a "Callstack flamechart" track beneath its Callstacks track. It draws every sample's stack along the timeline, so you can see how a thread's behaviour changes over time, not just the aggregate. Frames can be coloured by function or by code mapping (library), and clicking a frame shows its details. - **pprof:** step through multi-profile pprof archives with the arrow keys, and copy profile names. - **Heap dumps:** ART heap dumps can be exported as pprof from the flamegraph Export menu (including in Heap Dump Explorer), and Heap Dump Explorer flags classes potentially merged by R8. *Sampled callstacks over time: the new Callstack flamechart track under surfaceflinger's main thread, with the flamegraph for an area selection and the new Flamegraph / Call Tree / Functions tabs below.* *Call Tree view (top-down, fully expanded) for the same selection: total and self CPU time for every frame.* *Functions view: self and total CPU time per function, summed over every call path.* ## 🕸️ Flows that scale to dense graphs Selecting a slice in a trace with a dense flow graph (build system dependency traces are a common example) used to make the UI follow the entire flow chain, which could grind it to a halt. Many people have hit this over time ([#1004](https://github.com/google/perfetto/issues/1004)). - **Show only direct flows:** a new setting on the [Settings page](https://ui.perfetto.dev/#!/settings) that, when enabled, shows only the flows directly connected to the selected slice (one step) instead of the whole chain. - **Off by default:** existing behaviour is unchanged unless you turn it on. ## 💻 A friendlier Trace Processor CLI - **Readable SQL errors:** SQL errors are now laid out like rustc diagnostics, with a `--> source:line:col` location naming where the SQL came from (query, module, macro or metric), a line-number gutter and a caret. - **Markdown output:** `trace_processor query --format markdown` prints compact markdown tables, with configurable `--max-rows`, `--max-bytes` and `--max-cell-width` limits. - **Agent mode:** when run by a coding agent (detected from environment variables such as `CLAUDECODE` or `AI_AGENT`) with stdout not a terminal, results default to markdown and errors become single-line JSON. Force it on or off with `--agent` / `--no-agent`. - **Interactive shell:** prints aligned tables and shows the result of every statement, not just the last one. - **Progress and colour:** terminal-aware progress reporting, `--no-progress`, and `NO_COLOR` / `FORCE_COLOR` support. *Trace Processor CLI: a rustc-style error for a misspelled column, then query results printed as a markdown table with `--format markdown`.* [Learn more about agent mode](https://perfetto.dev/docs/reference/trace-processor-cli#agent-mode) ## 🧠 Memory: `linux.smaps` data source traced_perf can now record `/proc/pid/smaps` for selected processes, once or periodically. Processes can be selected by cmdline and uid range. The record page can also capture smaps snapshots alongside ART heap dumps. ## 🔍 Symbolization without local binaries Native profiles from Linux machines often arrive without the unstripped binaries needed to symbolize them. Trace Processor can now fetch debug files from [debuginfod](https://sourceware.org/elfutils/Debuginfod.html) servers by build ID, so `trace_processor bundle --debuginfod input.pftrace output.tar` produces a symbolized bundle with no local binaries at all. - **Opt-in and local-first:** lookups only happen with `--debuginfod`. Servers come from `--debuginfod-urls` or `DEBUGINFOD_URLS`, and local binaries are always tried first. - **Cached:** downloads are cached for later runs (`--debuginfod-cache-path` to override), with configurable connection and stall timeouts. - **Much less work:** mappings are now deduplicated across processes, so large traces send far fewer requests to llvm-symbolizer. - **Clearer results:** accurate counts of resolved and unresolved frames, `--verbose` to see every lookup, `--quiet` for scripts, and a clean error instead of a crash when llvm-symbolizer can't be run. - **samply profiles:** unsymbolized Firefox Profiler (samply) profiles can now be symbolized with `bundle`. [Learn more about symbolization](https://perfetto.dev/docs/learning-more/symbolization) ## 🐍 Python: connect to warm sessions `TraceProcessor(remote='my-session')` connects to a running `trace_processor server unix` session, so you can parse a large trace once and query it from many scripts. Only `query()` is supported over Unix sockets for now. `remote` also accepts HTTP addresses, and `addr` is deprecated in its favour. ## 🖥️ UI Enhancements - **Zoom to slice:** double-click a slice to select and zoom into it. - **Track groups:** "Expand all" / "Collapse all" in the track menu, and Shift+click on a group header to expand or collapse everything below it. - **Android:** frame timeline tracks are grouped by layer, and the AndroidLockContention plugin is revamped. - **Aggregations:** CPU slice aggregations gain a "CPU Time / Wall Time" column. Thread slice aggregations gain optional process, thread and track columns, and drill-downs open in a new tab. The old Pivot Table tab has been removed in favour of slice aggregations. - **Permalinks:** workspaces are now saved in permalinks. - **Robustness:** the timeline recovers from WebGL context loss, and two-finger horizontal scrolling no longer triggers browser back/forward on ChromeOS, Linux and Windows. - **Embedding:** embedders can stream traces over postMessage as a ReadableStream and use the new `shareable` / `downloadable` flags (see the compatibility notes below). ## ⚡ Trace Processor & SQL standard library - **New modules:** `android.process_state` (process and freezer state, exit reasons), `android.lock_held`, `android.cpu.cluster_utilization`, `android.job_scheduler_states_track_events`, `std.gpu.vulkan_debug_names`, plus `android_cuj_blocking_calls`. - **Wattson:** now supports Tensor G6 (CPU, GPU and TPU), MT6789, and Linux devices identified by their device tree. - **Importers:** perf.data imports handle fork and exit records and thread-scoped PMU counters. The strace importer works with real `strace -f` / `-T` output. - **Performance:** faster ART hprof import with lower peak memory. SQLite upgraded to 3.53.4. ## 🚂 Tracing Service and Probes - **GPU:** per-draw-call GPU render stage slices (`GpuRenderStagesConfig.drawcall_stages`). - **Compression:** compressed traces keep the clock snapshot, trace config and UUID uncompressed, so on-device tools can inspect them. - **Robustness:** the service now rejects producers with an unusable shared memory buffer instead of crashing. Fixed heapprofd unwinding on x86_64. ## 🧩 SDK improvements - **Data loss detection:** detect data lost to shared memory exhaustion with `TraceContext::drop_count()` (C++) / `PerfettoDsTracerGetDropCount()` (C). - **Flush info:** C SDK data sources can read the flush reason and flags. - **Big-endian:** big-endian support in the in-process SDK. - **Android Java SDK:** only allowlisted apps can register with the system tracing service. ## 🔧 Build - **New GN args:** `perfetto_cxx_standard`, and `perfetto_use_system_{re2,zstd,linenoise,expat}`. - **Bazel:** Perfetto can be used as a non-root Bazel module. ## ⚠️ Migration and compatibility notes Perfetto v59 includes a few changes worth checking when upgrading: - **postMessage traces:** traces posted to the UI as a bare ArrayBuffer are now local-only by default. Use the new `shareable` / `downloadable` flags (which replace `localOnly`) to control this. - **Graph functions:** `graph_reachable_dfs` / `graph_reachable_bfs` now return the start nodes when the graph has no edges, instead of an empty table. See [PerfettoSQL backwards compatibility](https://perfetto.dev/docs/analysis/perfetto-sql-backcompat). - **Shell commands:** the `.dump`, `.load-metrics-sql` and `.run-metrics` interactive shell commands have been removed, and `.width` and `-W/--wide` are deprecated and no longer do anything. Use `trace_processor export sqlite` instead of `.dump`. ---- A huge thanks to everyone who contributed to making Perfetto v59 possible.
